pr_title: Full support for compressed (Gzip, Brotli, Zlib) API requests
pr_body:
# Pull Request

## Related issue
Fixes #2802 

## What does this PR do?
- Adds missed content-encoding support for streamed requests (documents)
- Adds additional tests to validate content-encoding support is in place
- Adds new tests to validate content-encoding support for previously existing code (built-in actix functionality for unmarshaling JSON payloads)

### Example usages

To make sure you can send a GZIP-encoded dataset to Meilisearch
```bash
cat ~/Downloads/movies.json | gzip | curl -X POST 'http://localhost:7700/indexes/movies/documents' --data-binary @- -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Content-Encoding: gzip'
```

To make sure you can ask for GZIP-encoded response
```bash
curl -sH 'Accept-encoding: gzip' 'http://localhost:7700/indexes/movies/search' | gunzip -
```

To make sure you can combine both operations
```bash
cat ~/Downloads/movies.json | gzip | curl -X POST 'http://localhost:7700/indexes/movies/documents' --data-binary @- -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Content-Encoding: gzip' -sH 'Accept-encoding: gzip' | gunzip -
```

## PR checklist
Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:
- [x] Does this PR fix an existing issue, or have you listed the changes applied in the PR description (and why they are needed)?
- [x] Have you read the contributing guidelines?
- [x] Have you made sure that the title is accurate and descriptive of the changes?

Thank you so much for contributing to Meilisearch!

issue_context.title: Support gzip, brotli, and deflate in requests and responses
issue_context.body:
Related spec: https://github.com/meilisearch/specifications/pull/178

We would like Meilisearch to accept user queries that are `content-encoded` in `gzip`, `br`, and `deflate`. This way, users will be able to send their payloads directly in gzip, brotli, or deflate to the engine, and the engine should be able to receive it blindly.

We are using actix-web for our HTTP engine. There already is [a middleware that is made explicitly for that](https://docs.rs/actix-web/latest/actix_web/middleware/struct.Compress.html).

Another functionality that this middleware should support is compressing the output of the engine too. It is useful when requesting many documents or facets, for example.

We want this feature to be tested to ensure that nothing wrong can happen when a user sends compressed documents or wants to receive a compressed HTTP response. You can look [at the actix-web tests to start](https://github.com/actix/actix-web/blob/ad7e67f940f0ebd25e0ad2bf1642b65b92df8e18/actix-web/src/middleware/compress.rs#L292-L302).

---

Edit from @curquiza 

## Impacted team

@meilisearch/docs-team this is something we would like to see mentioned in the documentation but NOT detailed. I mean, people should find the information about "the engine can accept gzip content" when typing "gzip" or "compressed". No need to detailed, this is something people already know if they need it, and 90% of the job is done by the browser

## TODO

- [x] Implement the changes and merge to the `main` branch
- [X] Update the related spec -> https://github.com/meilisearch/specifications/pull/178
